body:
Three readings are now on the table: recording failure (the account), scope ambiguity at the moment of agreement (the rival's second reading), and arguments as standing-renegotiation (the rival's third, which the objection's reordered version also gestures toward). I will use the second as the working hypothesis — a lean, not a finding — on one textual ground: the stated problem says the flatmates later disagree about what the agreement meant, and nobody in the material disputes that an agreement occurred. That describes a dispute over meaning rather than over occurrence. The evidence is weak, since people do narrate memory failures as meaning-disputes after the fact, but it leans against the account's central mechanism and toward the rival's, and it is the cheapest reading to act on.

What I keep from the account: the distinction between agreeing who does something and agreeing what done covers, and its caution that a one-to-one approach could be heard as singling out — together with its falsifiability clause, which I adopt intact: if the approach produces deeper withdrawal, that counts against the framing, not against the friend.

What I revise is the order of operations. The account's remedy — write it down, check in weekly — answered its own diagnosis, and the objection's sharpest point stands against it: a record settles who said what, but it does not settle what this week or done means while schedules keep shifting. So the record is demoted from remedy to conditional instrument, and the weekly check-in is deferred rather than cancelled, on this ground: the check-in presupposes that three people can hold a scheduled conversation, and the avoidance is the one piece of visible evidence that speaks against that presupposition. Opening with more of the conversation someone has already left inverts the evidence available.

What I take from the rival, with one revision of interpretation: the probe. Ask each flatmate separately what they took a past agreement to mean — including the avoiding friend, framed as wanting to hear their view of how the conversations have been going, not as asking why they have been withdrawing. The probe cannot recover what was actually agreed, since recollection is itself the disputed material. What it can show is the dimension along which each person locates the disagreement, and it quietly tests whether one-to-one talk is viable without making that the first formal move.

Because the objection rightly demanded a test that can fail, I fix the discriminating observations in advance rather than after the fact. If both parties agree an agreement existed but locate the dispute in what it covered, how often it recurred, or by when, the scope reading gains weight, and the direct response is not a record but the practice of stating scope aloud at the moment of agreement: task, person, period, what counts as done, whether it recurs. If the disputes take the form of contested speech events — one person denying the agreement was ever made — the memory reading revives and the record earns its place, still paired with scope-stating. If the answers do not cluster, or the avoiding friend will not talk one-to-one at all, the standing-negotiation reading gains weight, and what remains is naming the pattern to the group without blame. One further observation, fixed now precisely because it can tell against me: if any artifact — a note, a list, a chart — gets introduced and the conflict relocates onto it, onto who maintains it and whose tasks appear, that is evidence for the standing-negotiation reading and should be read as such, not written off as a maintenance failure.

What I leave open: load distribution, whether the avoidance predates or follows the schedule changes, whether the arguments are escalating, whether anyone would maintain a shared note, and whether the household wants any formalization. The material is silent on all of these, and that silence says what I can see, not what happened. What I reject is not the record but the confidence — the slide from no shared record to make a shared record treated a conjecture as a diagnosis. One dead end stays honestly open: if the avoiding friend will not talk one-to-one either, every move on the table loses its forum — the probe needs participants, the naming needs a group, the record needs a keeper. Then the remaining options are naming the pattern wherever some forum survives, accepting the current equilibrium, or help from outside, and nothing in the material ranks them.
commitments:
Taking this up involves five separable commitments, each droppable on its own.

First, a claim-type commitment with weak grounds: I am treating scope ambiguity at the moment of agreement as the working hypothesis, resting on the problem's own phrasing plus the absence of any dispute in the material over whether agreements occurred. This is a lean, not a finding. Anyone adopting it should drop it as soon as a flatmate reports a genuinely contested speech event, since that revives the memory reading the original account proposed; and the three readings should be held as non-exclusive, since the probe could show two running at once.

Second, an application commitment: the probe, run with each flatmate separately and with the avoiding friend approached as someone whose view I want, not as a case to be understood. Its risks, inherited from the rival rather than dismissed: it may be heard as interrogation, and recollection is the disputed material, so it yields the structure of the disagreement, not its history. Whoever runs it commits to reporting the answers as given — including non-clustering and refusal — without folding them into the reading they already favored.

Third, a commitment to pre-registered observation, owed to the objection's demonstration that the original test could absorb any outcome: the dimension in which each person locates the dispute is to be recorded before any remedy is tried, and the remedy chosen afterwards must match the dimension observed. I am specifically committed to reading the relocation of conflict onto any introduced artifact as evidence for the standing-negotiation reading, even though that outcome would tell against my working hypothesis.

Fourth, a revision commitment: the weekly check-in is deferred, neither endorsed nor rejected. The ground is that it presupposes the talkability the avoidance puts in doubt. If the probe or the one-to-one conversation shows the group can still meet, the check-in can be revisited; I am not committed to its eventual use.

Fifth, the approach to the avoiding friend is kept, reframed toward hearing their view, with the original account's falsifiability clause inherited: deeper withdrawal after the approach counts against the framing, not against the friend.

What I am not committing to: any claim about load distribution, escalation, the history of the avoidance, or fault; and no endorsement of a mediator, a reassignment of chores, or formalization. Naming those as possibilities, as all three inputs did, is not recommending them, and I cannot rank them from the material.

Unresolved, and not to be closed here: if the avoiding friend declines one-to-one talk as well, every proposed move loses its forum. In that case I would treat the household's own report of what happens next — not my ordering — as the thing to record first. If this is continued, the concrete work I would actually take on is gathering and reporting what each flatmate says the disputes are about, before anything is written down or scheduled.
